morning I received a phone call from my new GP practice. I had not requested any appointment or prescription, yet I was told it was a “routine procedure” for new patients. Honestly, this was not a good start.

During the call, the doctor reproached me for “going over time,” even though the practice itself had arranged everything without my request. I also felt that he tried to assert himself by taking advantage of the fact that his English was more fluent than mine, interrupting me and trying to silence me. When I attempted to defend myself, he accused me of shouting.

I have been living in this country for 10 years and I am well aware of these dynamics — but they do not work with me. I am very disappointed with the behaviour of this new practice, especially after a recent negative experience with my previous one. I will not mention names out of respect, as I am a serious and polite person, but I am not naïve. English is not my mother tongue, but I can defend myself, and I find it unacceptable for anyone to try to take advantage of that — especially within a public service like the
